input.question: Why is it, that with bad (mobile) Internet reception, advertisements are often displayed perfectly while normal content seems to have "trouble"?
input.ground_truth: The page is hosted on a server somewhere and the adds are drawing information from a different server. If the server hosting the webpage is slower than the ad host, then the adds can load before the page content. This effect can be removed by manually changing load order for the page, placing advertisements at the bottom of the load order, to ensure that your content shows up first. There are some online advertising companies that gather information when their ads are displayed and they can really slow down a site. These adservices require that they load first, and they bog down the site with the data collection making the rest of the load order take forever. Try something like adblock and see if it clears up the loading problems. As a final option, it could always be malware.

I am a man.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it, that with bad (mobile) Internet reception, advertisements are often displayed perfectly while normal content seems to have "trouble"?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you are trying to watch your favorite cartoon on your tablet, but the Internet is slow and not working well.

Now, think of the Internet like a little delivery truck that brings things to your tablet. The truck brings two kinds of things: **ads (advertisements)** and **the real video or pictures you want to see**.

Here’s why ads show up even when the Internet is bad:

1. **Ads are small and simple.**  
   Ads are like tiny pictures or short videos. They don’t have a lot of details, so the delivery truck can bring them quickly, even if the road (the Internet) is bumpy.

2. **The things you want (like videos) are big and heavy.**  
   The real show or website you want is like a big, heavy box. It has lots of details and colors, so the delivery truck struggles to bring it fast when the road is bad.

3. **Ads are stored nearby.**  
   Sometimes, the ads are already saved on your tablet or very close to it (like in a special box nearby). So even if the Internet is slow, the tablet can show the ad quickly from that box.

4. **Websites want you to see ads.**  
   The people who make the websites really, really want you to see their ads, even if the Internet is slow. So, they make sure the ads always try to come through, no matter what.

So, when the Internet is bad, the little ads can still get to you, but the big, fancy things you want take longer or don’t work as well!
